candidates.summary: Anthropic announces Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, available now.
facts: Anthropic page: Fable and Mythos are the same underlying model; Fable has cybersecurity and biology safeguards so it is available to all users.
Anthropic page: outputs up to 30% faster than Fable/Mythos 5.1; price $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens.
Anthropic page: optional fast mode speeds token generation up to 2.5x, at $16 / $80 per million tokens.
Anthropic page: for most coding and knowledge tasks it recommends starting with Claude Opus 5.5; Fable 5.2 can act as Advisor or Orchestrator.
Anthropic page: during prerelease testing it formalized the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours.

candidates.summary: ClaudeDevs posts a guide on which Claude model to build with: when to use Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet or Haiku, when to adjust effort instead of switching models, and how to save cost by putting subagents on smaller models.

Alex Albert shares the prompt he runs on all his projects with every new model: "Read this entire project and find everything that’s broken, inconsistent, inefficient, or no longer needed. Fix what you’re sure about and list the rest for me to review."

Matt Pocock's tip for AI 'grilling' sessions: explain the 'why' instead of the 'what'. Bad: "I want to build an analytics panel for admins with graphs and filters". Good: "Admins can't currently see an overview of the important data in the app".
Theo reports Fable 5.2 built a project in 76 minutes for about $42 in tokens, and says it was not significantly better than Opus 5.5 (especially for the price).
Alex Finn describes using Fable 5.2 (early access) for all planning and brainstorming, iterating on an idea until it is ironed out, then having it create detailed tasks in a task manager.

Kun Chen shares a prompt to try on Fable 5.2: "audit and find implicit state machines in this <codebase/directory/module> that would drive concrete improvements if made explicit. explain before/after of each one and discuss with ..." (post text truncated in the read).
Guillermo Rauch says he is bullish on MCP and that a missing piece was how to get arbitrary callbacks across sessions; post text truncated at 'MCP could read and ...'.

Alexandr Wang announces Meta's smallest model yet, Muse Ember: 'nearly Muse Spark 1.3 (max) intelligence at a 17x cheaper price point (per AA)'; first model trained using Muse Wonder Full; available via API and muse code. Follow-up posts: matches Haiku at 3x cheaper cost per task; $0.10 / $0.50 per Mtok.

OpenAI says it built Control Room, a central system to track model workloads across its research infrastructure and stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise; it connects every research inference workload including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation.

The Verge runs an explainer, 'Everything we know so far about the Nvidia spy scandal targeting CEO Jensen Huang'. Same story is covered today by Stratechery ('Jensen Huang's Affair, The Culper Report, Huang's Righteousness'), Gary Marcus ('Jensen is cooked'), MIT Technology Review ('an Nvidia investigation') and a second Verge piece. Bodies not read; headline-level.
Ethan Mollick publishes 'Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI' on One Useful Thing. Headline-level; body not read.
MIT Technology Review: 'The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity'. Headline-level; body not read.
